title: ⌘K palette: a record-share hit is still titled by the raw recipient id, because sys_record_share is titled by the polymorphic text field recipient_id (follow-up to #34175)
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZiaBg6rk7dpy1s9Me

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding owed by the L1 ACCEPT of PR #35292 (comment 6998964493, 范围外去向 (a)), from the #34175 os-dev report. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets lane and grade.

## What the user sees

In the ⌘K palette and global search, a `sys_record_share` hit is titled by a raw principal id (a user, role or group id), not by who the record is shared with.

## Why (read from source and the built spec; not measured at a public door)

- `sys_record_share.nameField` is `recipient_id`, a `Field.text` polymorphic principal id paired with `recipient_type`, not a lookup.
- PR #35292 (#34175) makes `searchAll` follow a reference-typed `nameField` (lookup / master_detail / user / tree) to the target's ADR-0079 title. A text field is not a reference, so this producer, which #34175 named, is not changed by that fix. `canServeApiOperation({ apiMethods: ['get','list'] }, 'search')` answers true, so the object is searchable.

## Fix direction (a different design from #34175)

Title the hit through a `recipient_type`-keyed directory read (user / role / group), the same read the console's recipient-picker face performs, run as the searcher, with the bare id kept for a refused reader (the #34175 rule).

## Reader

`packages/metadata-protocol` record reads (`domain:server`), or whoever owns the record-share surface.

Dedupe: open-issue search `record share palette title`, `recipient_id raw id`, `search title polymorphic recipient` → none.
